title: highFIS: High-Dimensional Takagi-Sugeno-Kang Fuzzy Inference Systems in Python
content: This paper introduces highFIS, an open-source Python package for training and evaluating high-dimensional Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) neuro-fuzzy inference systems. TSK systems are widely appreciated for their local linear approximation capabilities and structural transparency, yet the classical product T-norm formulation suffers from exponential rule activation collapse and softmax saturation in high-dimensional spaces. The highFIS library addresses this limitation by unifying thirteen high-dimensional TSK estimator families and a baseline model under a single declarative, scikit-learn-compatible application programming interface (API). These estimators leverage modern mathematical strategies to mitigate the curse of dimensionality, including antecedent exponent re-formulation, differentiable softmin approximations, adaptive parametric T-norms, double groups of gates for sparse feature and rule selection, and head-based subspace decomposition. Every family is implemented with both a Classifier and a Regressor variant that integrate naturally with the meta-estimators and model evaluation frameworks of scikit-learn. Built on PyTorch, the package en-ables efficient gradient-based optimization with hardware acceleration, offers extensive introspection utilities to extract interpretable rule bases, and supports versioned checkpoints for model persistence. Usage is illustrated on a low-dimensional interpretability example and on real high-dimensional classification and regression datasets.
